LESSON: ORAL LITERATURE 4.1.1 SHORT FORMS OF ORAL LITERATURE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experiences Sugg
Topic 4.1: Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature, part of Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experiences Sugg in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do the short forms of oral literature help in enhancing creativity and imagination?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the types of short forms of oral literature for literary appreciation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. analyse the features and functions of each of the short forms of oral literature for literary analysis,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. compose short forms of oral literature for effective performance,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the roles of short forms of oral literature in the society.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. describe the types of short forms of oral literature for literary appreciation,

   Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. analyse the features and functions of each of the short forms of oral literature for literary analysis,

   Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. compose short forms of oral literature for effective performance,

   Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the roles of short forms of oral literature in the society.

   Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on the types of short forms of oral literature (e.g. proverbs, riddles, tongue twisters, jokes, puns),

2. watch performances of the different forms of oral literature. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view,

3. discuss the meanings and features of the short forms of oral literature and present their findings in class. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication, be given more considerable time or be provided with alternative corresponding activities,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on the types of short forms of oral literature (e.g. proverbs, riddles, tongue twisters, jokes, puns),
2. watch performances of the different forms of oral literature. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view,
3. discuss the meanings and features of the short forms of oral literature and present their findings in class. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication, be given more considerable time or be provided with alternative corresponding activities,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: This is enhanced as learner work with peers to compose, review and perform

short forms of oral literature.

● Citizenship: This is developed as the learner engages with others to discuss various aspects of short forms of oral

literature.

Values:
● Social justice: This is enhanced as the learner harmoniously interacts with peers to compose, review and perform short

forms of oral literature,

● Integrity: This is fostered as the learner chooses to practise self-discipline during the discussion, creation and

performance of short forms of oral literature.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates with others during discussions to create the short forms of oral

literature.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. describe the types of short forms of oral literature for literary appreciation,
2. analyse the features and functions of each of the short forms of oral literature for literary analysis,
3. compose short forms of oral literature for effective performance,
4. appreciate the roles of short forms of oral literature in the society.

Remember the key question: How do the short forms of oral literature help in enhancing creativity and imagination?
